[i]3000 Words[/i]]

Südoffensive-Zentrale Militärkommission

The Central Military Commission of the Technokratisches Kaiserreich, June 18th 2005

Under the orders of the Kaiser and in pursuit of the predestined inheritance of the Hochdeutsch peoples, the Zentrale Militarkomission began to plan for an invasion of the southern city states by 2005. The Hochdeutsch Empire had lost control of the region in the early 1900s after the Great Civil War and the fall of the monarchy to socialist control. In this time a series of city states had been established by locals including the states of Eustroa and Panesa. When the new Kaiser was crowned in 2001, the Empire would set its sights on reclaiming its southern territories. Long considered one of the great humiliations of the Hochdeutsch people, the Kaiser established the reclamation of the southern territories as a nonnegotiable part of national rejuvenation. Once negotiations had broken down in 2003 over the annexation of Panesa with the Panesan government, the Reichswehr began to mass at the border with Panesa. Lines of tanks including the Reichsadler Mark 45 approached the southern border. DF-21 ballistic missiles in the southern reaches of Imperial territory began to be fueled. In January of 2004, the Reichswehr would begin to cross into northern Panesa. The much smaller armies of Panesa would be quickly overrun by Reichswehr forces. Air engagement between the Panesan Air Force(PAF) and the Kasierluftwaffe would be limited as paveway bombs struck PAF aircraft before they were able to scramble from their runways. At sea, the limited PA forces were driven back and decisively defeated in the Battle of Mittelelseyr. DF-21 ballistic missiles soared overhead and struck major cities in Panesa before the government capitulated and surrendered after twelve days of fighting. 

A special meeting of the standing committee of the Hohenrach de Reiches would be called on June 7th to June 11th of 2005 on the annexation of Panesa. The ruling Peoples Stability Party or the Partei für Volksstabilität would be split on whether to create a friendly puppet state or to completely annex. The big tent nature of the PfV would create divisions between the old guard and reformists who prioritized less of a war hawk route. Following days of negotiation within the party, the PSP leadership would decide upon a timeline for the annexation of Panesa and its associated territories. By 2009 they would agree that the territory would be completely annexed into the Empire on top of spending around $16 billion to rebuild the territory after the war. Majority leader Frederick Stahl of the PfV would approve the Neudresden Protocol for consideration by the Kaiser and the Central Military Commission. Following debate in the cabinet the Protocol would eventually be adopted by the government in June 29th, 2005. To compromise with the reformist wing of the PfV, certain changes to the military conscientious objector law would be adopted as a widely recognized exchange for the Protocol to pass the Hohenrat de Reiches. Major industrial activity in Panesa would be limited to state-owned corporations until 2010 for the purposes of national security. During this time the territory would be divided into three corps tactical zones and the local government would be purged by security forces. While the majority of Panesan resistance had been suppressed by the Reichswehr in the initial invasion, there would still be fights against the Panesan partisans who continued to sabotage Kaiserreich holdings and operations in the territory. 

The national destiny ordained by the Kriegskult is being fulfilled with the Neudresden Protocol. To bring Eleysr under Hochdeutcsh control is the goal set forth by the Kaiser and we shall march towards it. This Protocol backed by the PfV will secure the future of the Panesan and Hochdeutsch people and defeat the insurgents.

- Excerpt from a speech by Frederick Stahl of the PfV on the Neudresden Protocol. 

On January 2nd, 2006 in Neudresden groups of Panesan partisans would stage a terrorist attack at the King Frederick Hoch Deutsch Bahn Station. A group of Panesans disguised as immigrants had entered the Schäfer-Bahnhofshalle in the early morning during commuter hours. Using a series of improvised explosive devices placed within various locations they would kill around 31 commuters and injure another 56. The Neudresden Police Department would rule the attack as an extremist terror attack by the remnants of the Panesan partisans. In reaction, the Kaiserreich would increase the Reichswehr presence in Panesa in a period known as the surge. General Erich Vogel would be brought in from the northern command(NCOM) to deal with the situation. Insurgent warfare against the Panesans would be brutal. Entire villages would be wiped out in the drain the sea doctrine employed by the General. Entire towns and cities would be executed or forcibly removed to a different location to deny the enemy access to a supportive local populace. In their place, the Technokratisches government would support the movement of Hochdeutsch peoples into the newly established Secure Zones or Sicherheitszonen. However, the Technokratisches government along with the State Media companies such as Nationale Medien would suppress news of the atrocities. Journalists would not be permitted into the Special Panesan Districts and internet access would be heavily restricted and information would be censored. Even so, some news of the doings of the Reichswehr would make its way out of the area although it would be heavily distorted by the state. Nationalists within the Hohenrat de Reiches would compare the invasion of Panesa to that of the northern states that had forged the modern Hochdeutsch state often citing the textbooks many Hochdeutsch had grown up with;

As the Hochdeutsch stabilized internally they began to turn their attention outside of the Empire. Towards interior Eleysr which was rich in resources the newly established Kaiserliche Armee would face their first test. The Qashliq Khanat which had remained the rulers of the area since they pushed out the Regnozian Imperium had ruled for centuries. In 620 AD, the Kaiserliche Armee led by General Konrad Mayer would cross the River Nördlich into Khanate territory. Driving towards the Khanates capital of Qashliq the General would arrive in its outskirts within three weeks of march. Through a constant artillery bombardment the Hochdeutsch forces would crush the entrenched Qashliq forces and drive them out of the area. The General would pursue the Qashliq forces and the Khan further north to the reaches of the Ob steppes while leaving his subordinates to hold the city. As he and the Kaiserliche Armee marched north he would be ambushed by the Qashliq horde at the Battle of the Ob River. When the Kaiserliche Armee was attempting to cross the frigid river at a passing located in a valley they would be surrounded and attacked by the Khanate forces. Attempting to execute a fighting retreat the General would order his forces to cross to the eastern bank of the river. While attempting to swim across he would drown under the weight of his own chain mail. With leadership being removed the remaining forces were cut down by the Khanate. 

When news arrived to the occupying Fifth Armee in Qashliq of the Generals demise his subordinates would quickly burn down the city and retreat back across the Nördlich. Before leaving the city they would massacre its residents, loot its valuables and execute a fighting retreat back into Kaiserreich territory. Choosing not to pursue into Kaiserreich territory the Khan would remain on the eastern bank of the Nördlich. The disastrous outcome of the First Qashliq-Hochdeutsch war would lead to the Kaiser purging all commanders related to the military disaster.

1922 Invasion of Assace-Zorraine 

The region of the Assace Zorraine had long been a contentious point between the Hochdeutsch peoples in the south and the French states of the north. Assace-Zorraine had changed hands between various French and Hochdeutsch states over the centuries depending on their strength at the moment. The region, rich in resources, would be handed over and over again through war to the more militarily capable party. As the French state of the Republique de Valmont began to collapse after the Great Civil War, the Hochdeutsch Empire would see its opportunity to reclaim Assace-Zorraine. Initially, the First and Fourth Armed Corps would cross the Neu Rhine and begin their lightning offensive into Assace Zorraine. Encountering little resistance in the south they would advance to around 50 kilometers outside of the Valmont capital before being halted by Valmontese forces. The long guns of the Reichswehr would bombard the capital, destroying centuries of history and architecture. However, the Valmontese would begin pushing back the Hochdeutsch as their overextended supply lines began to result in a lack of supplies. Pulling back to the Assace-Valmont border, the Hochdeutsch forces would dig in along the tall river embankments of the Neu Rhine to prevent a Valmontese crossing. Similarly, the Valmontese would dig in several kilometers from the Hochdeutsch lines. Both sides would be locked in for several months through the winter as the ice and cold made advances near impossible. During this time millions on both sides would die from disease and starvation on top of violent deaths. 

Once the spring thaw began, the Hochdeutsch high command would embark on another ploy to break the stalemate. Hochdeutsch Corps would be issued chemical weapons including ammonia to use against the Valmontese lines. The initial use of the gas had a profound physical but also psychological effect on the Valmontese causing their lines to break after months of bitter struggle. Following the chemical attacks, the Hochdeutsch forces would advance for the first time in months although casualties would still be high. As they pulled back, the Valmontese forces would burn down silos, destroy farmland and poison wells. The scorched earth strategy would prevent Hochdeutsch forces from utilizing the local resources slowing their advance. The new motorized units of the Hochdeutsch Army which relied on petroleum had intended on seizing the oil fields to the north of Assace-Zorraine to fuel the war effort. However, after Valmontese generals had ordered the torching of the fields the advance of Hochdeutsch armor would grind to a halt. 

In the west, the campaign was doing better. The First Corps had surrounded a Valmontese force in southern Assace-Zoraine and forced their surrender. By June they had already advanced into Valmont itself. As they moved into the area they undertook a ruthless campaign against the Valmontese both military and civilian. The widespread massacres that were carried out during this area were sanctioned by the Kaiserliche Kriegskult or Imperial War Cult as necessary to prepare it for the Hochdeutsch settlements. By January of the next year, the Reichswehr had fully secured Assace Zorraine excluding a small pocket of Valmontese resistance in the far-east. During this time some members of the Hochdeutsch war council advised the Kaiser to end the war and take the territorial gains. However, the Kaiser insisted on continuing the war to push for the full destruction of the Valmontese state. The war was no longer about territory or power but rather the full destruction of Valmontese civilization. Backed by Kriegskult teachings that the Hochdeutsch peoples should be the only to populate Elseyr, the Reichswehr would continue to push into Valmont. By this time Valmontese forces had become completely exhausted. A quarter of fighting age men in the country had already been killed, the populace was starving and the once glorious capital had been bombed into ruin. By the end of January the Valmontese government had surrendered to the Hochdeutsch Empire in a capitulation known as the Humiliation of the River Tren named for the place where the accords were signed. 

Second Qashliq-Hochdeutsch War(added from last expansion cause it didnt get included)

In 632 AD, to restore the honor of the Kaiserreich the Kaiser ordered another military campaign against the Khanate. First, they would move south to cut off the vassals of the Khan, defeating the Manstyi at the Battle of Irman and subjugating them. Then crossing the River Nördlich again, they would defeat the Khan in August of 634 at the Battle of the River Nördlich through use of superior artillery and maneuvering tactics by the Kaiserliche cavalry. As the Khanate horde pulled back from the River the Kasierreich cavalry corps would quickly flank and surround them. Slow moving foot soldiers would then follow and deliver the final blow to the Khan. Around 27,000 Khanate soldiers and 15,000 Kasierliche Armee forces would be killed during the battle, wiping out the majority of the Khans fighting forces. When the sons of the Khan attempted to proclaim the continuation of the Khanate, the Kaiserliche Armee would march on Qashliq one last time. Upon reaching the city the Armee proceeded to quickly crush the remaining weakened Qashliq Khanate forces and kill the successors of the Khan in their own palace. 

Settlement of Östliche Provinzen

Upon the deposition of the Khanate, the Imperial Government in Neudresden would proclaim the new imperial province of Ostliche Provinzen or the Eastern Province. A series of expeditions into the area by imperial cartographers would map out the area for further expansion, settlement and exploitation of local resources. By the thousands the citizens of the Kaiserreich would move into the Eastern Province and displacing the local population of Qashliq. Incidents of violence between the settlers and the native Qashliq would become common-place as the two groups disputed over land and resources. The doctrine of the Kriegskult proclaimed that the Ostliche Provinzen was divinely mandated to the Hochdeutsch people and its settlement was integral to the greatness of the Hochdeutsch people. The Kaiser, an extreme expansionist, would strongly support settlement efforts into the northeast. It was proclaimed that any male citizen of the Reich over twenty years of age would be granted free land in the east if he was able to properly settle the area. An initial fifty acres would be given for free and an extra twenty would be given for every family member he brought with him. A series of conflicts between the native Qashliq and the Hochdeutsch would flare up in the eastern reaches of the Ostliche Provinzen. Following a skirmish that killed twenty Hochdeutsch settlers, the Kaiserliche Armee would be called forth by the Kaiser. The mandate would be to remove or kill every Qashliq in the entirety of the Empire for they stood in front of the divine mandate given by the Erster Kaiser. During this time the Kaiserliche Armee would carry out massive atrocities against the native population. Eventually of the eighteen million Qashliq, eleven million would be removed from the Empire and expelled to the north. Two million would be killed by the Kaiserliche Armee with the Kaiserreich additionally cutting off food supplies to majority Qashliq areas. The remaining Qashliq would be rounded up by the settlers and Kaiserliche Armee and placed on Indian reservations in the far rural reaches of the province where they wouldnt be able to effect the rest of the Hochdeutsch Empire. 

Erster Südenkrieg

The Erster Südenkrieg or First Southern War was a series of unsuccessful military campaigns between the Kaiserreich and the lowland or tiefland nations to the south. As settlers moved to the Ostliche Provinzen the Kaiserliche Armee high command or Kriegskommand would turn its eyes southwards. During the collapse of the Regnozain Imperium portions of Valentia Maritima would break off from the central Stahlbasin authorities and form a confederation of city-states and petty kingdoms. They would remain largely untouched during the civil war between the Hochdeutsch as military campaigns turned inwards between the city-states of the north. However, as the centralized state restrengthened it turned its eyes to reuniting itself with the Tiefland. 

By the 750s, nearing the end of the Early Imperial Era, the major lowland nations were composed of Vandermere, Brennsland, Ostmere and Fensbruck. Vandermere and Ostmere bordered the westernmost portions of Ostliche Provinzen and were susceptible to an initial Kaiserliche Armee assault. Overnight in August of 753 the Kaiser ordered the 3rd and 2nd Kaiserliche Armee units to cross into Vandermere territory. The vastly outnumbered Vandermere, he assumed, would fall quickly. The armies stormed the capital city within hours and occupied the area. However, the occupation effort would be greatly damaged by the constant sabotage and elusive rebels in the rural areas of Vandermere. When a coalition of Tiefland nations composed of Ostmere, Brennsland and Vandermere rebels formed to oust the Kaiserreich the Kaiserliche Armee would pull out of Vandermere. 

In 757 AD, the Kaiserreich returned to Tiefland. This time they resorted to scorched earth tactics to subjugate the Vandermere peoples. The Kriegskommand would contribute significant resources to combating rebels and any Vandermere citizens suspected of aiding anti-Kaiserreich causes would be put to death. Most of the population through the course of half a decade would be relocated to Sicherheitszones or safe zones which were heavily fortified and regulated urban areas which Kaiserliche Armee officers controlled. During this time the Vandermere would be a military governed zone under martial law where Generals were given total command to do what they wished to defeat the rebels. By 773 the area was determined to be pacified and was then fully annexed into the Kaiserreich. 

Zweite Südenkrieg

The Zweite Südenkrieg would come in 789 AD. Following the subjugation of Vandermere, the Kriegskommand had established an alliance with the Tiefland nation of Fennsbruck. However, when King Elsje de Bruin died in 788, his son, would terminate the alliance with the Kaiserreich on the grounds of preventing further expansionism into the Tiefland. The second Armee would be dispatched to the border between Vandermere and Fennsbruck, armed with newly acquired artillery. The cannons, armed with gunpowder from the oriental east, would be used to pound Fennsbruck with continuous artillery fire. For seven days the barrage would continue with cannonballs flying across the border into the Fennsbruckian capital. In the end the city would be laid to waste and the Kaiserliche Armee would pull back, determining that the cost of occupation would be too great. From 789 to the early 1900s the Tiefland would remain largely independent of the Kaiserreich.

[quote=alkiragunya;59742464][SpoiLEr="Smiles" and fragments, Arc of the lost totem-3]
[i]Ooo Ngarrajin, não vai ir lá com o resto do grupo não?[/i]
Foi oque Tjarrampa perguntou ao ir até Ngarrajin, o qual estava reclinado em uma árvore, pensativo, ele olhou para Tjarrampa, olhos cor de âmbar, ele sorriu sutilmente atrás de sua máscara, e então acenou em concordância, Tjarrampa deu lhe um sorriso de aprovação.
[i]Isso aí, tem que tentar ficar mais junto de nós, eu sei que você pode ser assim mais introvertido, mas, não lhe impede de ficar junto lá, qualquer coisa me avise![/i]
Tjarrampa disse, ele puxou Ngarrajin de seu repouso, o mascarado apenas o seguiu, eles ficaram sentados ao redor da fogueira, lá estavam, além deles dois, Kialja, Gillut e Tomboon estavam lá, na fogueira Dulbara e Unbaranga lidavam com a preparação da comida, o aroma de larvas tostadas e frutas torradas domina o ar, alem de uma sensação de calmaria inconfundível causada por Tomboon.
[i]Veja a arte de cozinhar![/i]
Disse Dulbara enquanto com espetos, feitos por Unbaranga, virava a carne com uma mão e com a outra manipulava o fogo.
[i]O fogo cozinha excelentemente o exterior, mas cuidado para não deixarem o interior cru![/i]
Após algum tempo, a carne do lagarto ficou bem assada.
[i]Toma Equid(Unbaranga)[/i]
Disse Dulbara passando um lagarto para Unbaranga fatiar, ele o fez, tornou seus dedos em espinhos pontiagudos e começou a fatiar a carne do lagarto, após terminar, ele espetou a carne em seus dedos e os desfez, caindo em pedaços no tronco que estava preparando a carne, ele passa para Tomboon passar a carne, já que logo Dulbara já passou mais um para Unbaranga cortar.
[i]Toma mais um Equid[/i]
...
[i]E mais um...mais esse, e ....esse daqui[/i].
[i]Você não precisa falar enquanto me passa a carne sabia...[/i]
Unbaranga disse, com um tom leve de incômodo que logo se desfez por Tomboon, que disse.
[i]Calmem, estamos no espírito de festa ainda e de comer, não de brigar[/i]!
Ele disse ativando o Pirpiri, todos lá ficaram mais calmos e até mais...libertos, por um instante o sorriso de Tomboon, típico, caiu, ele pegou um pedaço de perna de lagarto para disfarçar.
Enquanto Tomboon intervinha, Ngarrajin apenas havia pegado uma faca de ossos de um tronco próximo, ele poderia usar os próprios dedos como um Nynghna, mas optou por não fazer, ele descascou alguns quandongs de seu próprio manto, comeu alguns e ofereceu outros à Tjarrampa e Kialja, ele não removeu a bandana para comer, apenas passou a mão por baixo e começou a devorar a fruta.
[i]Por que você é tão desesperado em não mostrar a própria face? até Gillut mesmo comendo como um animal não esconde.[/i] 
Gillut olha para Kialja enquanto devora um pedaço de carne de lagarto que nem foi assado.
[i]Eu escutei isso[/i].
Kialja apenas riu de leve, e voltou a Ngarrajin
V[i]ocê é nosso amigo, mercante, não precisa-[/i]
Tjarrampa irrompeu entre ambos de repente, claramente viu que essa conversa levaria a algo bem desconfortável e que Ngarrajin não gostava de falar sobre, Tjarrampa afinal, o conhecia desde que eram amigos de infância.
[i]EI, vocês viram como essas larvas desse ano não parecem boas como às do ano passado?[/i]
Kialja pareceu confusa, mas entendeu que aquilo poderia ser desconfortável para Ngarrajin,  o qual suspirou de alívio, eles seguiram uma conversa casual...
Após a situação na fogueira acalmar, Tomboon saiu de lá , queria descansar um pouco, Mardu o viu porém, e o parou se colocando em sua frente.
[i]Tomboon, seu espírito parece...mais pesado que o comum[/i].
Mardu questiona, ele não estava olhando para quem estava a sua frente, mas sim a alma de Tomboon, a essência de seu ser, parecia, pesar.
[i]Eu estou bem, Mardu, mas, há coisas que...é melhor não se falar sobre.[/i]
Mardu o observou com cuidado por alguns segundos, ele respeitou sua decisão em não falar e o deixou passar, mas o mistério persiste, Nghayhl surgiu por trás de Mardu, colocando a mão em seu ombro, seu corpo curvado pela idade, e falou:
[i]Os Bangwopa carregam um fardo maior que muitos clãs, seus membros são exatamente como os quokkas, mesmo no mais árido e inóspito ambiente sorriem, mesmo na pior seca, eles se mantém assim, sorridentes...mas suas almas, elas choram por dentro.[/i]
Nghayhl dizia, mesmo que Tomboon já tivesse ido em outro canto mais distante, Mardu acenou em concordância, não falou mais nada, e então ambos foram para seus gunyas.
Kialja estava indo de atrás de Tamboon, ela usava um manto de penas sagradas, em um gesto de amigável, ela arrancou uma das penas e entregou à Tamboon, dizendo:
[i]Amigo, olhe essa pena, acho que combina com você![/i]
Tamboon sorriu, e agradeceu a Kialja, ele pôs a pena em seu cabelo pelo restante do dia.
Quando o sol começou a ese esconder no horizonte, as crianças correram para seus gunyas, um deles, neto de Kambilla, Bingaray, tropeçou em um vaso de cerâmica, e o quebrou, o garoto correu para o gunya de seu avô, que por sorte já estava dormindo, mas ele não viu que entre os fragmentos do vaso se encontrava um pedaço de algo...brilhante, era um pedaço de madeira curvo e que pulsava uma sutil energia espiritual, Ngarrajin, que estava acordado até tarde, sentiu, e foi até lá, catou os cacos do vaso e então fez um breve feitiço, [i]dispersão[/i], ele falou, a areia sob seus pés se desfez, e então ele colocou os pedaços do vaso lá, antes de reverter a magia no entanto e fazer a areia voltar ao normal, ele sentiu um objeto emanando a mesma energia que o mesmo que ele havia encontrado no  deserto, ele pegou o objeto e fez um breve gesto que enterrou os fragmentos do jarro.
[i]Juntar isso...hmm, isso é a traseira, e essa é corcova...seria esse[/i].
Os olhos de Ngarrajin brilharam, aquele deveria ser o totem perdido a tanto tempo do clã Murkitilpa, ele guardou os dois pedaços porém, preferindo o deixar até o amanhecer.
[b][i]Bocejo[/i][/b] [i]vamos logo Ngarrajin amanhã tu limpa bagunça das crianças, bora dormir logo.[/i]
Tjarrampa disse chegando de repente pondo a mão no ombro de Ngarrajin, ele parecia com sono e seus movimentos meio desengonçados, Ngarrajin sorriu sutilmente por trás de sua bandana e acenou que sim. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[i]Ooo Ngarrajin, aren't you going there with the rest of the group?[/i]
That's what Tjarrampa asked as he walked over to Ngarrajin, who was reclining in a tree, thoughtful, he looked at Tjarrampa, amber eyes, he smiled subtly behind his mask, and then nodded in agreement, Tjarrampa gave him a smile of approval. [i]That's right, you have to try to stay closer to us, I know you can be more introverted, but, it doesn't stop you from staying there, if anything happens, let me know![/i]
Tjarrampa said, he pulled Ngarrajin from his rest, the masked man just followed him, they sat around the fire, there were, besides the two of them, Kialja, Gillut and Tomboon were there, at the fire Dulbara and Unbaranga were dealing with the preparation of the food, the aroma of toasted larvae and roasted fruits dominates the air, in addition to an unmistakable feeling of calm caused by Tomboon.
[i]Look at the art of cooking![/i]
Dulbara said while with skewers, made by Unbaranga, he turned the meat with one hand and with the other manipulated the fire. [i]The fire cooks the outside excellently, but be careful not to leave the inside raw![/i]
After some time, the lizard meat was well cooked.
[i]Take Equid (Unbaranga)[/i]
Dulbara said, passing a lizard to Unbaranga to slice, which he did, turning his fingers into sharp thorns and starting to slice the lizard meat, after finishing, he pricked the meat on his fingers and undid them, falling into pieces on the log where he was preparing the meat, he passed it to Tomboon to pass the meat, since Dulbara soon passed another one to Unbaranga to cut.
[i]Take another Equid[/i]
...
[i]And one more... another one, and... this one here[/i].
[i]You don't need to talk while you pass me the meat, you know...[/i]
Unbaranga said, with a slight tone of annoyance that was quickly dispelled by Tomboon, who said.
[i]Calm down, we're still in the party spirit and we're eating, not fighting[/i]!
He said, activating the Pirpiri, everyone there became calmer and even more... freed, for a moment Tomboon's typical smile fell, he picked up a piece of lizard leg to disguise himself.
While Tomboon intervened, Ngarrajin had simply picked up a bone knife from a nearby trunk, he could have used his own fingers like a Nynghna, but he chose not to, he peeled some quandongs from his own cloak, ate some and offered others to Tjarrampa and Kialja, he didn't remove his bandana to eat, he just put his hand underneath and began to devour the fruit.
[i]Why are you so desperate not to show your face? Even Gillut, even when eating like an animal, doesn't hide it.[/i]
Gillut looks at Kialja as he devours a piece of lizard meat that hasn't even been cooked.
[i]I heard that[/i].
Kialja just laughed lightly, and turned back to Ngarrajin.
[i]You're our friend, merchant, there's no need to-[/i]
Tjarrampa suddenly burst in between them, clearly seeing that this conversation would lead to something very uncomfortable and that Ngarrajin didn't like to talk about, Tjarrampa, after all, had known him since they were childhood friends. [i]HEY, did you see how this year's larvae don't look as good as last year's?[/i]
Kialja looked confused, but understood that this could be uncomfortable for Ngarrajin, who sighed in relief, they continued a casual conversation...
After the situation at the bonfire calmed down, Tomboon left there, he wanted to rest a little, Mardu saw him however, and stopped him by standing in front of him.
[i]Tomboon, your spirit seems...heavier than usual[/i].
Mardu questions, he wasn't looking at who was in front of him, but rather Tomboon's soul, the essence of his being, seemed to weigh. [i]I'm fine, Mardu, but there are things that...are better not to talk about.[/i]
Mardu observed him carefully for a few seconds, he respected his decision not to speak and let him pass, but the mystery persists, Nghayhl appeared behind Mardu, placing his hand on his shoulder, his body bent with age, and spoke:
[i]The Bangwopa carry a greater burden than many clans, their members are exactly like the quokkas, even in the most arid and inhospitable environment they smile, even in the worst drought, they remain like that, smiling...but their souls, they cry inside.[/i]
Nghayhl said, even though Tomboon had already gone to another, more distant corner, Mardu nodded in agreement, said nothing else, and then they both went to their gunyas. Kialja was walking behind Tamboon, she was wearing a sacred feather cloak, in a friendly gesture, she plucked one of the feathers and gave it to Tamboon, saying:
[i]Friend, look at this feather, I think it suits you![/i]
Tamboon smiled, and thanked Kialja, he put the feather in his hair for the rest of the day.
As the sun began to set on the horizon, the children ran to their gunyas, one of them, Kambilla's grandson, Bingaray, tripped over a ceramic vase, and broke it, the boy ran to his grandfather's gunya, who luckily was already asleep, but he didn't see that among the fragments of the vase there was a piece of something... shiny, it was a piece of wood curved and pulsating with a subtle spiritual energy, Ngarrajin, who was awake late, felt it, and went there, picked up the shards of the vase and then cast a brief spell, [i]dispersion[/i], he said, the sand beneath his feet fell apart, and then he placed the pieces of the vase there, before reversing the spell however and making the sand return to normal, he felt an object emanating the same energy as the one he had found in the desert, he picked up the object and made a brief gesture that buried the fragments of the jar.
[i]Put this together...hmm, this is the back, and this is the hump...that would be it[/i].
Ngarrajin's eyes shone, that must be the long-lost totem of the Murkitilpa clan, he kept the two pieces however, preferring to leave it until dawn. [b][i]Yawn[/i][/b] [i]Let's go Ngarrajin, tomorrow you can clean up the kids' mess, let's go to sleep soon.[/i]
Tjarrampa said, arriving suddenly, putting his hand on Ngarrajin's shoulder, he looked sleepy and his movements were a bit clumsy, Ngarrajin smiled subtly behind his bandana and nodded.

[Spoiler=Entre memórias e pedaços, Arco do Totem Perdido-4, capítulo 4]
Após o sol nascer no horizonte, e todos iam acordando e saindo de seus gunyas, a primeira e mais notável coisa foi, Kambilla vendo o vaso estilhaçado nas areias. Bingaray parecia meio encolhido, mas seu avô parecia, não se importar muito.
[i]Oque já aconteceu já foi, não há motivo para lhe punir por isso.[/i]
Bingaray parecia surpreso, e então gaguejou:
[i]E-então não vai me punir por isso?![/i]
Kambilla apenas suspirou, parecia meio melancólico e não estava a  fim de se importar com isso, ele apenas disse:
[i]Não...agora pode ir.[/i]
Com um simples gesto de mãos, fez a areia cobrir novamente os cacos, e se certificou de pegar uma pedra próxima para cobrir o local, Kambilla liberou Bingaray, que apenas saiu para outro lugar com outras crianças. Recostado em uma árvore, Ngarrajin via a situação se resolvendo, ele estava em conflito se deveria ou não revelar a Kambilla sobre o totem fragmentado, por fim, o mercador decide se mover em direção a ele.
[i]Oque você quer comerciante, trouxe alguma mercadoria de longe?[/i]
Ngarrajin acenou que não, e falou com a voz abafada:
[i]Mas, interessante.[/i]
Ele retirou de seu manto os dois fragmentos, os olhos de Kambilla brilharam, em um vislumbre de esperança, ela o pôs em sua mão, sentindo a energia pulsante, mas, algo parecia...faltante.
[i]Isso é...incrível, mascarado, mas como você...[/i]
Ngarrajin apontou ao deserto.
[i]Achei por aí.[/i]
Ele falou, e então saiu sem dizer mais nada, Kambilla ficou lá, em choque, mas empolgado por finalmente conseguir algo, então ele percebeu.
[i]Está...faltante, faltam pedaços, o totem deveria...estar completo, mas não está...[/i]
Kambilla decide ir até Balunji para receber respostas.
Ao ir ao centro do assentamento, onde Balunji estava, viu ele, Gillut e Tjarrampa jogando [b]Kalka[/b].
(* Kalka é um jogo que consiste no seguinte, os jogadores recebem três ossos, um representa Wonambi[água], Dingo[Fogo] e Canguru[Terra], quem conseguir alinhar os 3 símbolos primeiro, ganha.)
[i]Quero ver algum de vocês ganharem de MIM[/i].
Gillut disse, preparando a última pedra, se ele acertasse essa, ele ganharia o jogo. Ao jogar, ele murmurou.
[i]Gurraba[/i]
Ao lançar a pedra, uma nuvem de poeira se formou do impacto, em formato de camelo,  quando abaixou, as pedras estavam estilhaçadas em um formato que lembrava um camelo incompleto.
[i]Mas que-[/i]
Gillut disse confuso, Balunji logo disse o repreendendo.
 [i]GILLUT, isso é uma JOGO, e NÃO DECLARAÇÃO DE GUERRA!

[/i]
Tjarrampa que viu a nuvem e o formato de pedras riu levemente e disse:
[i]Bem, pelo menos tivemos essa arte formada por esse Gurraba...[/i]
Mas o conflito se dispersou, quando Kambilla surgiu entre o grupo, com urgência em seu tom, deu a Balunji os dois fragmentos.
[i]O mercador encontrou isso, partes de nosso [u]totem perdido[/u][/i]
Balunji logo se virou ao seu lado mais sério para analisar os fragmentos, sua mão direita, que tinha um espiral gravado, brilhou em um tom colorido, mas, meio desbotado.
[i]Wonambi confirma a legitimidade, mas, ele está...incompleto, de alguma forma.[/i]
[i]Um totem? Incompleto? Como assim![/i]
A resposta de Balunji deixou Kambilla com mais dúvidas que respostas, ele o respondeu de forma clara.
[i]Totems podem ser partidos, mas para quebrar eles sem destruir o vínculo entre o clã e a magia ancestral exigiria uma habilidade e precisão muito...humanos, não nego a possibilidade de que o deserto tenha o quebrado, mas é improvável.[/i]
Balunji murmurou algo, baixo, e então estendeu os fragmentos para Kambilla, antes que pudesse formular uma resposta, um orbe colorido com um mapa da região surgiu.
[i]Hm? Aparentemente, os dois fragmentos restantes devem estar no local marcado. [/i]
Tjarrampa reconhece o local imediatamente, ele fala:
[i]Nariburu?[i]Eu conheço esse lugar,  eu e o Ngarrajin sempre nos encontrávamos lá quando crianças, fica ao leste, seguindo a songline de meu clã.
NGARRAJIN, lembra da caverna das mariposas?[/i]
Tjarrampa grita para Ngarrajin, que estava ajudando Unbaranga cortar carne, ele se virou e fez um sinal de positivo com a mão em direção ao amigo e voltou a trabalhar. 
[i]Se não foi magia ancestral quebrando o totem só pode ter sido mãos humanas, haha, isso será divertido.[/i]
Gillut disse parecendo empolgado, Kambilla começou a falar novamente, não disfarçando sua urgência.
[i]Precisamos ir a Nariburu logo[/i].
Balunji levantou a mão com a palma aberta para que Kambilla se calasse.
[i]Compreendo sua preocupação, e ela é por um bom motivo, mas não podemos ser tão rápidos, é Tjarrampa quem conhece esse caminho e é ele quem irá nos guiar.[/i]
[i]Hm, se me permitem, eu vou lá comer um pouco, podem ir discutindo a logística aí, os camelos, comida etc...[/i]
Tjarrampa disse forçando um sorriso, ele só queria ir até Ngarrajin na verdade, ao chegar lá, convidou seu amigo:
[i]Ei, Rajin(Ngarrajin), vai querer ir com a gente lá pra Nariburu e encontrar os dois últimos fragmentos do clã Murkitilpa? Você é forte cara, pode nos ajudar bem lá, e também, voltaríamos a infância...[/i]
Ngarrajin sorri e acena que sim, e solta até uma risada, rara, e meio sem graça, Tjarrampa lança um sorriso largo ao ouvir essa risada põem o braço por trás dos ombros de Ngarrajin.
[i]Ahaha, que bom ouvir isso, lembra daquela vez que...[/i]
----------------------------------------------------------
[b]Flashback, Ngarrajin e Tjarrampa crianças.[/b].
[i]EU PEGUEI EU PEGUEI[/i]!
Tjarrampa gritou para Ngarrajin ao pegar uma mariposa grande cinza de penas brilhantes brancas, Rajin correu para o amigo e colocou o inseto em um jarro, Rajin exclamou animado com o amigo.
[i]TÔ AQUI TJAR![/i]
[i]EHEEHAW[/i]
Rajin riu, Tjarrampa pegou o jarro, os dois saíram da caverna, para querer se mostrar mais, Tjarrampa subiu em uma pedra mais alta e levantou o jarro para o alto, antes de poder falar qualquer coisa, seu pé escorregou da pedra, e ele caiu sobre Rajin.
[b]AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAGH[/b]
Os dois gritam, o vaso se quebrou no chão e quebrou em vários cacos, a mariposa se libertou e voou para longe.
[i]A QUALÉ-[/i]
Tjarrampa reclamou ao ver o inseto voando livre novamente.
---------------------------------------------------------------
[i]NGARRAJIN TJARRAMPA, não vem??[/i]
Balunji diz aos dois que estavam já à horas relembrando histórias.
[i]Nós já vamos partir logo, vamos.[/i]
....
------------------
After the sun rose on the horizon, and everyone was waking up and leaving their gunyas, the first and most notable thing was, Kambilla seeing the shattered vase on the sands. Bingaray seemed a little cowered, but his grandfather didn't seem to care much.
[i]What's already happened is done, there's no reason to punish you for it.[/i]
Bingaray seemed surprised, and then stammered:
[i]S-so you're not going to punish me for this?![/i]
Kambilla just sighed, he seemed a little melancholic and didn't want to care about it, he just said:
[i]No... now you can go.[/i]
With a simple gesture of his hands, he made the sand cover the shards again, and made sure to grab a nearby stone to cover the spot, Kambilla released Bingaray, who just went off to another place with other children. Leaning against a tree, Ngarrajin watched the situation resolve itself, he was conflicted about whether or not he should tell Kambilla about the fragmented totem, finally, the merchant decided to move towards him.
[i]What do you want, merchant, did you bring some merchandise from far away?[/i]
Ngarrajin shook his head, and spoke in a muffled voice:
[i]But, interesting.[/i]
He removed the two fragments from his cloak, Kambilla's eyes shone, in a glimmer of hope, she put it in her hand, feeling the pulsating energy, but, something seemed... missing.
[i]This is... incredible, masked, but how did you...[/i]
Ngarrajin pointed to the desert.
[i]I found it around there.[/i]
He spoke, and then left without saying anything else, Kambilla stood there, in shock, but excited to finally get something, then he realized. [i]It's...missing, there are missing pieces, the totem should...be complete, but it's not...[/i]
Kambilla decides to go to Balunji to get answers.
When she went to the center of the settlement, where Balunji was, she saw him, Gillut and Tjarrampa playing [b]Kalka[/b].
(* Kalka is a game that consists of the following, the players receive three bones, one represents Wonambi[/water], Dingo[Fire] and Kangaroo[Earth], whoever manages to align the 3 symbols first, wins.)
[i]I want to see one of you beat ME[/i].
Gillut said, preparing the last stone, if he hit this one, he would win the game. As he threw, he muttered.
[i]Gurraba[/i]
When he threw the stone, a cloud of dust formed from the impact, in the shape of a camel, when he lowered it, the stones were shattered in a shape that resembled an incomplete camel.
[i]What the-[/i]
Gillut said confused, Balunji soon said reprimanding him.
[i]GILLUT, this is a GAME, and NOT A DECLARATION OF WAR!

[/i]
Tjarrampa who saw the cloud and the shape of stones laughed lightly and said:
[i]Well, at least we had this art formed by this Gurraba...[/i]
But the conflict dispersed, when Kambilla appeared among the group, with urgency in his tone, he gave Balunji the two fragments.
[i]The merchant found this, parts of our [u]lost totem[/u][/i]
Balunji soon turned to his side more seriously to analyze the fragments, his right hand, which had a spiral engraved, shone in a colorful tone, but, somewhat faded. [i]Wonambi confirms the legitimacy, but it is... incomplete, somehow.[/i]
[i]A totem? Incomplete? What do you mean![/i]
Balunji's answer left Kambilla with more questions than answers, he answered him clearly.
[i]Totems can be broken, but to break them without destroying the bond between the clan and the ancient magic would require very... human skill and precision, I do not deny the possibility that the desert broke it, but it is unlikely.[/i]
Balunji muttered something, quietly, and then held out the fragments to Kambilla, before he could formulate an answer, a colored orb with a map of the region appeared.
[i]Hm? Apparently, the two remaining fragments should be in the marked location. [/i]
Tjarrampa recognizes the place immediately, he says:
[i]Nariburu?[i]I know this place, Ngarrajin and I always met there when we were kids, it's to the east, following my clan's songline.
NGARRAJIN, remember the moth cave?[/i]
Tjarrampa shouts to Ngarrajin, who was helping Unbaranga cut meat, he turned and gave a thumbs up with his hand towards his friend and went back to work.
[i]If it wasn't ancient magic breaking the totem it must have been human hands, haha, this will be fun.[/i]
Gillut said looking excited, Kambilla started talking again, not hiding his urgency.
[i]We need to go to Nariburu soon[/i].
Balunji raised his hand with an open palm to make Kambilla shut up.
[i]I understand your concern, and it is for good reason, but we cannot be so quick, it is Tjarrampa who knows this path and he is the one who will guide us.[/i]
[i]Hm, if you will allow me, I will go there to eat a little, you can discuss the logistics there, the camels, food, etc...[/i]
Tjarrampa said with a forced smile, he only wanted to go to Ngarrajin in fact, when he got there, he invited his friend:
[i]Hey, Rajin (Ngarrajin), do you want to go with us to Nariburu and find the last two fragments of the Murkitilpa clan? You are strong man, you can help us well there, and also Also, we would go back to childhood...[/i]
Ngarrajin smiles and nods yes, and even lets out a rare and somewhat awkward laugh. Tjarrampa smiles broadly upon hearing this laugh and puts his arm around Ngarrajin's shoulders.
[i]Ahaha, that's good to hear, remember that time when...[/i]
----------------------------------------------------------
[b]Flashback, Ngarrajin and Tjarrampa as children.[/b].
[i]I CATCHED IT I CATCHED IT RAJIN QUICKLY[/i]!
Tjarrampa shouted to Ngarrajin as he caught a large gray moth with shiny white feathers. Rajin ran to his friend and put the insect in a jar. Rajin exclaimed excitedly with his friend.
 [i]I'M HERE TJAR![/i]
[i]EHEEHAW[/i]
Rajin laughed, Tjarrampa took the jar, the two left the cave, wanting to show off more, Tjarrampa climbed onto a higher rock and lifted the jar high, before he could say anything, his foot slipped off the rock, and he fell on Rajin.
[b]AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAGH[/b]
The two screamed, the vase broke on the ground and broke into several pieces, the moth broke free and flew away.
[i]AAAAAAAAAA  WHY[/i]
Tjarrampa complained when he saw the insect flying free again.
---------------------------------------------------------------
[i]NGARRAJIN TJARRAMPA, aren't you coming??[/i]
Balunji told the two that they had been remembering stories for about a few hours.
[i]We're going to leave soon, let's go.[/i]
....
